'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir]]
**Three civilians are killed by suspected [[Islamic extremism|Islamist terrorists]] at three different locations in [[Srinagar]], [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]], in a spike of killings targeting civilians in the area. The victims were a [[Hinduism|Hindu]] chemist, an [[India]]n [[street food]] vendor from [[Bihar]], and a [[Islam|Muslim]] [[Taxi|taxi driver]]. Two other civilians were killed in Srinagar four days ago by a [[Lashkar-e-Taiba]]-linked group. [https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/srinagar/prominent-kashmiri-pandit-businessman-shot-dead-in-srinagar-7554192/ (''The Indian Express'')]
*[[Afghan conflict|Afghanistan conflict]]
**A report by [[Amnesty International]] says that the [[Taliban]] has [[capital punishment in Afghanistan|executed]] 13 [[Hazaras]], including eleven former members of the [[government of Afghanistan|government]], shortly after the [[Fall of Kabul (2021)|fall of Kabul]]. The Taliban denies that they were behind the killings. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/5/taliban-killed-13-members-of-hazara-ethnic-group-report (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*Russian actress [[Yulia Peresild]] and [[film director]] [[Klim Shipenko]] launch into space onboard [[Soyuz MS-19]] from the [[Baikonur Cosmodrome]] in southern [[Kazakhstan]]. They intend to film scenes for ''[[The Challenge (2022 film)|The Challenge]]'', which will be the first feature-length movie filmed in outer space, on the [[International Space Station]] over one week before returning to [[Earth]]. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/10/05/russian-crew-blast-off-to-film-first-movie-in-space-a75211 (AFP via ''The Moscow Times'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Evergrande liquidity crisis]]
**Two further [[China|Chinese]] real-estate developers, [[Fantasia Holdings]] and Sinic Holdings, with liabilities of [[United States dollar|$]]12.8 billion and $14.2 billion respectively, both fail to make bond payments amid tightening resource availability after [[Evergrande]] raised investor concerns, and were both downgraded to "CCC" or "substantial credit risk". [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/10/05/china-property-default-risk-for-fantasia-sinic-amid-evergrande-crisis.html (CNBC)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Romania]]
****[[Romania]] reports a record 15,037 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,289,156. [https://www.romania-insider.com/index.php/ro-covid-cases-oct-5-2021 (''Romania Insider'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 895 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 211,696. [https://interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/72811/ (Interfax)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Spain]]
****The [[Ministry of Health (Spain)|Ministry of Health]] announces that the National Public Health Commission will offer booster doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] beginning in late October to elderly people who received their second vaccine dose at least six months ago. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-10-spain-over-70s-dose-covid-vaccine.html (MedicalXpress)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria]]
*****[[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] reports a record 1,763 new cases and four deaths in the past 24 hours, which is the highest daily total reported by any [[Australian state]] since the start of the pandemic. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-10-05/victoria-records-new-covid-cases-vaccine-progress/100513784 (ABC News Australia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in New Zealand]]
****[[Prime Minister of New Zealand|Prime Minister]] [[Jacinda Ardern]] announces the details of the [[Immunity passport#COVID-19|COVID-19 vaccine certificate]]s, which show full vaccination status, in order to make large-scale events safer. The vaccine certificate is expected to come into use in November. [https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/new-zealand/vaccine-certificates-in-use-summer-ardern (TVNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
***[[Singapore]] reports a record 3,486 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 109,084. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/community/nine-people-aged-between-64-and-90-die-of-complications-linked-to-covid-19-in (''The Straits Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Zambia]]
***[[Zambia]] lowers its [[COVID-19 vaccination in Africa|vaccination]] target from 70% to 30% in December as the country will relaunch the nationwide vaccination program on Thursday. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/zambia-lowers-covid-19-vaccination-target/2382699 (Anadolu Agency)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Afghanistan–United Kingdom relations]]
**UK special envoy [[Simon Gass]] meets with Taliban Deputy Prime Ministers [[Abdul Ghani Baradar]] and [[Abdul Salam Hanafi]] in Kabul for the first time since the [[2021 Taliban offensive|takeover of the country]] to discuss [[Afghanistan]]'s growing humanitarian crisis and terrorism, and to guarantee safe passage to those wishing to emigrate. Taliban Foreign Ministry spokesman [[Abdul Qahar Balkhi]] also said they discussed the possibility of restoring diplomatic relations, with Gass saying the foreign ministry wishes to "begin a new chapter of constructive relations". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/5/british-pms-envoy-holds-talks-with-taliban-in-afghanistan (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Two prison guards are taken hostage at a prison in [[Condé-sur-Sarthe]], [[Normandy]], [[France]]. One of the hostages is injured. The hostage-taker later surrenders. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/two-guards-taken-hostage-french-jail-bfmtv-2021-10-05/ (Reuters)]
*A court in the [[Holy See]] agrees to return to the investigative phase of an ongoing trial against Cardinal [[Giovanni Angelo Becciu]] for alleged embezzlement, abuse of power and fraud, and other charges. Becciu was fired from his position in the [[Vatican City]] by [[Pope Francis]] in 2020 for alleged [[nepotism]], which Becciu also denies. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/prosecution-vatican-trial-acknowledges-defects-willing-investigate-more-2021-10-05/ (Reuters)]
*Nine [[barracks]] at the former [[Auschwitz concentration camp]], now the [[Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum]], are vandalized with [[Holocaust denial]] [[graffiti]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/anti-semitic-graffiti-discovered-at-auschwitz/ar-AAPayoF?ocid=uxbndlbing (MSN)]
*[[Office of the Prosecutor General of the Republic of Moldova|Prosecutor General of Moldova]] [[Alexandru Stoianoglo]] is suspended from his positions by [[President of Moldova|President]] [[Maia Sandu]], and is detained by security forces following allegations of corruption. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/moldovas-top-prosecutor-suspended-detained-corruption-case-2021-10-05/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Romanian political crisis]]
**The [[Cîțu Cabinet|Romanian government]] is dissolved following a [[no confidence vote]] against the centrist government of [[Prime Minister of Romania|Prime Minister]] [[Florin Cîțu]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/romanias-parliament-topples-pm-citus-centrist-government-2021-10-05/ (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Libyan general election]]
**The [[Libya]]n [[House of Representatives (Libya)|House of Representatives]] votes to postpone the parliamentary elections initially scheduled for December 24, alongside the presidential election, until January 2022. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/5/libya-legislative-elections-delayed-until-january-parliament (AFP via Al Jazeera)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Microsoft Windows version history]]
**[[Microsoft]] launches [[Windows 11]], its latest version of the [[Microsoft Windows]] [[operating system]]. The upgrade to Windows 11 will be free for [[Windows 10]] users. [https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-58795119 (BBC News)]
*Climatologists [[Syukuro Manabe]] and [[Klaus Hasselmann]] and [[theoretical physicist]] [[Giorgio Parisi]] are awarded the 2021 [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] for their work towards the understanding of [[physical system]]s through [[climate model]]s. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/nobel-physics-2021-syukuro-manabe-klaus-hasselmann-giorgio-parisi-winners-2564735 (AFP via NDTV)]
